review_notes: Read all 175 lines of Mathlib/Control/Traversable/Equiv.lean, and inspected the rules these declarations interact with: Mathlib/Control/Traversable/Lemmas.lean (attribute [simp] LawfulTraversable.id_traverse at line 37; attribute [functor_norm] LawfulTraversable.naturality at line 35; traverse_id/traverse_comp @[functor_norm] at lines 95-105), Mathlib/Control/Traversable/Basic.lean (class definitions, LawfulTraversable fields lines 221-237, ApplicativeTransformation preserves_* @[functor_norm] lines 128-140), Mathlib/Control/Functor.lean (Comp.map_mk @[functor_norm] line 172), Lean core Init/Control/Lawful/Basic.lean (attribute [simp] id_map line 45; Functor.map_map simp line 50; map_pure/seq_pure simp line 107), and the only in-repo users, Mathlib/Data/DList/Instances.lean lines 37-41 (Traversable DList := Equiv.traversable ...; LawfulTraversable DList := Equiv.isLawfulTraversable ...). Considered candidate annotations but rejected them for lack of support: (a) adding @[simp] to Equiv.id_map/Equiv.id_traverse is largely redundant for downstream users, since Equiv.traversable sets traverse := Equiv.traverse eqv (and Equiv.functor sets map := Equiv.map eqv), so the already-simp LawfulFunctor.id_map and LawfulTraversable.id_traverse for t' cover the same terms whenever LawfulTraversable t' is the transported instance (as in DList); (b) adding @[simp] to traverse_def (lines 100-102) would compete with the existing simp-elimination direction needed by id_traverse/traverse_eq_map_id and would expose the internal eqv.symm representation as a default normal form, and note that this rfl lemma is already picked up by dsimp as a definitional-equality theorem (Lean/DefEqAttrib.lean: 'A theorem with a definition that is (syntactically) `:= rfl` is implicitly marked `@[defeq]`'), so it is not unreachable; (c) Equiv.comp_map follows the core convention that comp_map is not simp while Functor.map_map is. The local simp calls in proofs (Equiv.map, traverse_def, functor_norm) are consistent with those sets' intended use. No replacement was compiled or tested; uncertainty remains about instance-transparency matching between Functor.map and Equiv.map, which could in principle make some proposed simp rule redundant or competing, but no concrete user-facing defect in the simp interface is evidenced by the sources read.
